title: The Trojan War
summary: A legendary ten-year siege of the city of Troy by a coalition of Greek kingdoms, sparked by the abduction of Helen, wife of the Spartan king Menelaus, by the Trojan prince Paris. The war is the central subject of Homer's Iliad and forms the backdrop for the Odyssey and much of later Greek heroic legend.

phases.title: The Judgment of Paris and the abduction of Helen
phases.description: The war's mythic origin traces to a beauty contest among three goddesses, judged by the Trojan prince Paris. He chose Aphrodite after she promised him the world's most beautiful woman, Helen, who was already married to Menelaus of Sparta.

phases.title: The Greek coalition gathers
phases.description: Menelaus's brother, Agamemnon, assembled a coalition of Greek kings and warriors, including Achilles, Odysseus, and Ajax. Bound by an earlier oath to defend Helen's marriage, they sailed for Troy.

phases.title: Nine years of siege
phases.description: The war ground on for years without a decisive breakthrough, marked by individual duels, raids on nearby settlements, and shifting fortunes on both sides.

phases.title: The Wrath of Achilles
phases.description: The central events of the Iliad begin with a dispute between Agamemnon and Achilles over a captive. Achilles withdraws from battle, causing severe consequences for the Greek war effort. The death of his close companion Patroclus draws Achilles back into the fighting, where he kills the Trojan hero Hector.

phases.title: The Trojan Horse and the fall of Troy
phases.description: Unable to breach Troy's walls by force, the Greeks followed Odysseus's plan. They built a massive wooden horse, hid warriors inside, and pretended to sail away. The Trojans brought the horse inside their walls. The hidden Greeks emerged at night, opened the gates, and destroyed the city.

sources: Virgil, Aeneid (for the Trojan Horse episode)
